ideas.name: Opening-range breakout
ideas.reason: Index prices tend to snap back within the day, which works against breakouts. It didn't survive costs.

ideas.name: Asian-range breakout
ideas.reason: Failed the four gates once an exit bug was fixed (the stop check started before the trade existed).

ideas.name: VWAP systems
ideas.reason: The profit came from a bug that put the stop on the wrong side of the entry. Fixed, nothing was left.

ideas.name: Trend-day entries
ideas.reason: Failed the four gates.

ideas.name: Tight-stop intraday entries
ideas.reason: Failed the four gates.

ideas.name: School-run (a mid-morning time-of-day pattern)
ideas.reason: Failed the four gates.

ideas.name: High-frequency reversal
ideas.reason: The profit per trade was too small to survive costs.

ideas.name: Overnight drift
ideas.reason: The profit per trade was too small to survive costs.

ideas.name: Cross-asset relative value
ideas.reason: Failed the four gates.

ideas.name: Session reversals
ideas.reason: Failed the four gates.

ideas.name: Breadth divergence
ideas.reason: Failed the four gates.

ideas.name: ICT 2022 model, coded as taught
ideas.reason: It lost money over 866 trades, and fake time windows did just as well.

ideas.name: ICT, optimised over 34,560 settings
ideas.reason: Tuned on past years and tested on the next one, it couldn't be told apart from luck. The chance the tuning was overfit: 51%.

ideas.name: ICT: volatile day + weekly trend + pullback
ideas.reason: Below the bar, and 92% of its profit came from shorting one index.

ideas.name: Leveraged-ETF rebalancing at the close
ideas.reason: Leveraged funds must trade at the close, but the effect showed up in the wrong markets, with the wrong signs.

ideas.name: Buyback blackout windows
ideas.key: wrong sign in all six markets
ideas.reason: Companies pause buybacks before earnings. Prices moved the opposite way to the prediction in every market.

ideas.name: Vol-target deleveraging
ideas.reason: It looked like a pass at t 3.07, but a plain 'price fell for 5 days' rule did better. It was ordinary short-term reversal.

ideas.name: Month-end FX hedge rebalancing
ideas.reason: Hedges should push prices in proportion to the month's move. They didn't.

ideas.name: Semi-monthly payroll
ideas.reason: If paydays drove buying, moving payday should move the effect. When it moved, the effect went negative.

ideas.name: 60/40 fund rebalancing
ideas.reason: Real in theory, but tiny next to normal daily price noise.

ideas.name: Treasury settlement calendar
ideas.reason: Worked in the years used to find it, then disappeared in the years after.

ideas.name: Quarter-end, December and Japanese fiscal-year seasonality
ideas.reason: None of the seasonal windows beat the rest of the year by more than luck.

ideas.name: Adding foreign bond markets to System A
ideas.reason: Every blend did worse than the US trade alone.

ideas.name: Treasury auction cycle
ideas.reason: The fake dates beat the real ones because they landed on month end. It was System A again.

ideas.name: Commodity index roll (the 'Goldman roll')
ideas.reason: A gold fund that never rolls futures showed the same pattern, so the roll wasn't the cause.

ideas.name: Monthly option expiry
ideas.reason: The fake week did better than expiry week.

ideas.name: Mid-month bond window
ideas.reason: Lost 85–90% of its return on years it hadn't seen.

ideas.name: Other index rebalances (MSCI, Nasdaq-100, S&P)
ideas.reason: Funds that don't track MSCI moved more on MSCI dates than the funds that do.

ideas.name: A within-month filter for System A
ideas.reason: Meant to improve System A. It cost money instead.

ideas.name: A month-end edge in Treasury bills
ideas.reason: The apparent edge was just the interest the bills pay.

ideas.name: Month-end bond buying in the last hour
ideas.reason: The buying doesn't bunch into the closing hour, so there's no sharper trade inside the day.

ideas.name: Pre-refunding Friday (confirm or kill)
ideas.reason: 75 of 96 events sat next to a month end. Away from month end it earned nothing.

ideas.name: Dividend-payment days
ideas.reason: Reinvested dividends were supposed to lift prices on payment days. Nothing since 2014.

ideas.name: Pension rebalancing into bonds
ideas.reason: No mark on bond prices, and the wrong sign at quarter ends.

ideas.name: 2-year vs 10-year month-end pair
ideas.reason: The 2-year leg earned everything and the 10-year leg lost it back.

ideas.name: Commodity hedging pressure (COT)
ideas.reason: Following producers' hedging positions lost money.

ideas.name: S&P 600 / 400 quarterly rebalance
ideas.reason: Lost money, and the fake dates did better.

ideas.name: CME bitcoin settlement hour
ideas.reason: Nothing around the settlement hour, in either direction.

ideas.name: Mortgage-bond payments on the 25th
ideas.reason: Its t above 3 came from month end again. Compared fairly, it was zero.

ideas.name: Crypto funding avoidance
ideas.reason: Real, but smaller than what a retail trader pays to trade it.

ideas.name: Pre-refunding drift in Treasuries
ideas.reason: The fake dates five sessions earlier earned almost as much.

ideas.name: Expiry-Friday spike
ideas.reason: It existed until about 2014, then it was gone.

ideas.name: Overnight drift before economic releases
ideas.reason: Gone after the paper that found it was published.

ideas.name: Announcement-day premium
ideas.reason: Announcement days used to be special. Since 2010, ordinary days earn more.

ideas.name: FOMC-cycle even weeks
ideas.reason: Reversed after it was published.

ideas.name: Pre-FOMC drift in Treasuries
ideas.reason: The fake dates five sessions earlier were just as strong.

ideas.name: FOMC announcement reversal
ideas.reason: Right direction, but eight meetings a year is too few to tell it from luck.

ideas.name: Quarter-start pension contributions
ideas.reason: If contributions drove System B, quarter starts should be strongest. They were the weakest.

ideas.name: Vol-target fund rebalancing
ideas.reason: Present all month, and weakest exactly where System B trades.

ideas.name: Buyback blackout
ideas.reason: The pattern ran backwards from what buybacks predict.

ideas.name: Dash for cash before month end
ideas.reason: The predicted dip before month end wasn't there.

ideas.name: Plain turn of the month, SPY alone
ideas.reason: On SPY alone, the plain version is no better than the middle of the month. A caution for System B.

ideas.name: Trend following, 12-month signal, 33 markets
ideas.reason: A real, well-known premium that fell just short of 2.8, and it needs about €20,000 with whole contracts.

ideas.name: Buying last month's biggest jumpers
ideas.reason: Ten names at a time, bought every month, lost almost everything deposited.

ideas.name: Insider purchase clusters
ideas.reason: Real but tiny since 2012, and costs ate it.

ideas.name: Post-earnings drift in microcaps
ideas.reason: The academic drift was there; a small account couldn't collect it after spreads.

ideas.name: Graham net-nets
ideas.reason: The closest call: the cheapest stocks did best, but the first half of the sample lost money.

ideas.name: Graham: P/E of 7 or less
ideas.reason: No better than random stocks of the same size.

ideas.name: Opportunistic insider purchases
ideas.reason: Rebalancing every month cost about 1% a month, more than any edge.

ideas.name: Piotroski F-score among cheap stocks
ideas.reason: The low scorers did better than the high scorers.

ideas.name: Graham's enterprising-investor screen
ideas.reason: Too few stocks passed all six tests to judge, and those lost money.

ideas.name: Microcap continuation after big moves
ideas.reason: The lead came from a flawed placebo. The frozen rule lost money in both periods.

note: 139 ideas are in the tally; the ones with their own write-up are listed here. Most of the rest were variants and quick checks of these.
